clue.text: Can stores change what we all have already?

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A puzzled shopper wonders whether tins and stores could change what everyone already owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone has forebears who lived before them, so all of us already have them.

clue.text: A deliberate pretence to lose at love

indicators.note: to lose says the word given by 'at' drops out of the longer word

parts.note: an affectation is a deliberately put-on manner, a pretence

explanation.surface: Someone feigns indifference to lose at the game of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness or tender feeling is a synonym for love.

clue.text: Agreement to mark time

explanation.surface: A pact is signed to tread water for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in harmony is an agreement, as in 'in tune'; a clock striking the hour marks time with bells.

clue.text: Wild ants? Not one in a tin-mine

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of 'ants' run riot into a new order

parts.note: nary is a dialect word meaning not a single one

explanation.surface: Feral ants are reported absent from a Cornish tin mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the insects' name; 'in' is only a link. The Stannaries were the tin-mining districts of Cornwall and Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stannary is a tin-mining district or the mine itself, from Latin stannum, tin.

clue.text: Hams finished by stray cats

parts.note: finished means over, as in 'the game is over'

indicators.note: stray suggests the letters of 'cats' wander out of order

explanation.surface: Hams left out are polished off by wandering cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hams' looks like meat for the cats but is a verb. 'stray' turns CATS into ACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates, so to ham is to perform too theatrically.

clue.text: Bit like coming up with the governor

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the joined words read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bit is a part
like means as

explanation.surface: Someone gets a small role resembling the arrival of the governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns PARTAS, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial ruler in ancient Persia.

clue.text: Only diamonds cover her

indicators.note: the two words cover a run of letters that spells a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman wears nothing but diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any 'her'.

clue.text: Glanced sideways, having shown the way round before

indicators.note: round says the guiding word goes round the word for before

parts.note: led means guided, shown the way
ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A guide looked sideways, having previously shown people round.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a sidelong, often lustful look is to ogle out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Went out around the interval and drove off

indicators.note: around says the word for went out encloses the word for interval

parts.note: a flame that went out died
a spell is a period or interval

explanation.surface: People went out for the interval and then drove away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish, as doubts or fears.

clue.text: Universal in approach to ale

indicators.note: in says the letter for universal sits inside the word for approach

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal approach tunnel into a mine
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A general way into a pub's ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: the word that goes with 'ale' to name a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Audit ale was a strong brew made at Oxford and Cambridge colleges for the day accounts were checked.

clue.text: Lot about to dress the ship

indicators.note: about says the word for lot goes round the word for dressing

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
to rig is to dress or fit out, especially a ship

explanation.surface: Plenty of people turn out to dress the ship with flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship of the sailing era, later an escort vessel.

clue.text: Locked! Charlotte may be back

indicators.note: back says the word suggested by Charlotte is read in reverse

parts.note: a charlotte is a pudding, a kind of sweet course

explanation.surface: A door slams; Charlotte may come back later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlotte' looks like a girl's name; it is the fruit pudding. 'back' turns DESSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Having locks of hair, or long ringlets, is having tresses.

clue.text: Neat point in class

indicators.note: in says the compass point sits inside the word for class

parts.note: a clan is a group or class of people
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A teacher praises tidy marks in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy means spotless, free from dirt.

clue.text: Humiliation at entertaining cads

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so 'at' wraps round the cads

parts.note: base men are low, dishonourable men, cads

explanation.surface: A host is mortified at having to entertain bounders.
explanation.definitionFit: Being brought low or degraded is a state of humiliation.

clue.text: Elected one in a county takes over

parts.note: a candidate elected is in

indicators.note: in says the numeral for one sits inside the county

parts.note: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newly elected official in a shire assumes control.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to property or a role, receiving it from a predecessor.

clue.text: Dignified treble, perhaps

explanation.surface: A dignified choirboy singing the top part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty in manner is dignified; a treble voice is pitched high in sound.

clue.text: Standard for a stone

explanation.surface: A flagpole's banner is the measure for a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner on a pole; a paving slab is a flagstone.

clue.text: Be not afraid of it, read Malvolio

definitions.text: Be not afraid of it, read Malvolio

parts.words: Be not afraid of it, read Malvolio
parts.note: in Twelfth Night Malvolio reads a forged letter: 'be not afraid of' a quality, for 'some are born' to it

explanation.surface: A line Malvolio reads aloud from a forged letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Malvolio is the pompous steward in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, tricked by a letter telling him not to fear eminence.
explanation.definitionFit: The forged letter's famous line concerns eminence: some are born to it, some achieve it, some have it thrust on them.

clue.text: Became enlarged, we hear, and rather horrible

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: grew some means became somewhat larger

explanation.surface: A swelling got bigger and quite ghastly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly and repellent, horrifying to look at.

clue.text: The artist wins at any time

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
e'er, ever, means at any time

explanation.surface: A painter is always winning prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals, who also made the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a celebrated Victorian painter.

clue.text: Name the chief Indian snake

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish chief or commander

explanation.surface: Identify the leading Indian snake.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian myth a naga is a serpent deity, and the word means cobra.

clue.text: Paper stamp for muslin

parts.note: a newspaper is a party's organ, its mouthpiece
a die is a stamp for striking coins

explanation.surface: Paper and a stamp are needed to send fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, stiff, translucent cotton, a kind of muslin.

clue.text: Religious garment on some in New York — capital!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the garment sits above the next word

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by priests
any means some

explanation.surface: A priest's vestment is worn by some New Yorkers, splendid!
explanation.walkthrough: Albany is the state capital of New York; 'capital!' also feigns being an old-fashioned exclamation of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of New York State is Albany.

clue.text: Party principles showing the right thing

explanation.surface: A party's manifesto proves just right.
explanation.definitionFit: In US politics a party's platform or slate is its ticket; 'just the ticket' means exactly the right thing.

clue.text: A William in the plot is a hanger-on

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the word for plot

parts.note: a site is a plot of land
William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A man named William in a conspiracy turns out to be a mere follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or dependant, as a moon is to a planet.

clue.text: Make sharp — the drinks are up

indicators.note: in a down clue, are up means the word for the drinks reads from the bottom

parts.note: ports are fortified wines

explanation.surface: Get ready: the drinks are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are up' reverses PORTS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop a razor is to sharpen it on a leather strap.

clue.text: Drank hard back in military HQ

indicators.note: back says the word for drank heavily is read in reverse

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol to excess

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking is reported at an army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base, storehouse or regimental headquarters.

clue.text: Goody-goody

parts.note: a goody-goody is someone sanctimoniously devout and virtuous

explanation.definitionFit: A goody-goody makes a show of being religiously virtuous.

clue.text: Absconded with wine as plunder

parts.note: absconded means ran away
sack is an old name for dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: A thief ran off with wine as loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search violently and rob, to pillage.

clue.text: Poet's to take the cork out, holds Love to be tedious

annotationWithheld.why: Poet's to take the cork out, holds Love to be tedious (7): OPE (poetic open) and O for love are clear, but no clue word gives the remaining R...SE letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Poet's to take the cork out, holds Love to be tedious

clue.text: Irishman growing rice

explanation.surface: An Irish farmer cultivating rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddy is a nickname for an Irish man; a paddy field is where rice is grown.

clue.text: Believers about — or speculators

indicators.note: about says the word for believers goes round the little word 'or'

parts.note: theists are believers in God

explanation.surface: Those with faith are around, or are they merely guessing?
explanation.definitionFit: Those who form theories are speculating thinkers.
